speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to pinpoint the underlying cause, have you ever smoked or been exposed to significant environmental irritants like dust or chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; your description of copious, thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum worsening in the morning, combined with a 11-year history of recurrent "bronchitis" in a non-smoker, is highly suggestive of a specific condition. To confirm this, I need to know if you have noticed any nasal discharge or if the cough ever improves significantly when you lean forward. Additionally, have you had any previous chest imaging, and if so, can you describe the findings? REQUEST IMAGES: Previous chest X-rays or CT scans.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The clinical picture of chronic productive cough, copious purulent sputum, and recurrent infections in a non-smoker is classic for this condition; the requested imaging would confirm dilated airways and the "tram-track" sign.
